facts.statement: Kumimanu lived approximately 56 to 60 million years ago during the Paleocene epoch.
facts.quote: Kumimanu is an extinct genus of giant penguin, which lived around 56 to 60 million years ago.

facts.statement: Fossils of Kumimanu were found in New Zealand and the discovery was announced in December 2017.
facts.quote: Fossils were found in New Zealand, and the discovery was announced in December 2017.

facts.statement: Researchers found Kumimanu fossils at Hampden Beach on the South Island of New Zealand.
facts.quote: The Kumimanu fossil material were found by a group of researchers from the Hampden Beach of Otago, on the South Island of New Zealand.

facts.statement: The Kumimanu fossils originate from the Paleocene Waipara Greensand formation.
facts.quote: The fossils are from the Paleocene Waipara Greensand.

facts.statement: A New Zealand and German team led by Gerald Mayr studied the Kumimanu fossils.
facts.quote: The fossils were studied by a New Zealand and German team, led by Gerald Mayr of the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum.

facts.statement: The genus name Kumimanu translates to "monster bird" in the Māori language.
facts.quote: The generic name Kumimanu means "monster bird" in Māori language

facts.statement: The species name biceae honors Beatrice A. Tennyson, the mother of author Alan J. D. Tennyson.
facts.quote: The specific name biceae honours Beatrice ("Bice") A. Tennyson who is the mother of one of the authors, Alan J. D. Tennyson.

facts.statement: The proposed species Kumimanu fordycei was named after a large specimen found by Alan Tennyson in 2017 from the late Palaeocene Moeraki Formation.
facts.quote: Kumimanu fordycei is named based on a large specimen from the late Palaeocene Moeraki Formation, dating to 55.5–59.5 million years ago. It was found by palaeontologist Alan Tennyson in 2017.

facts.statement: In 2025, Mayr et al. revised their findings to suggest that features distinguishing K. fordycei from K. biceae fall within the variation of a single species, identifying K. fordycei as a junior synonym of K. biceae.
facts.quote: In their 2025 description and revision of fossil material from the New Zealand Waipara Greensand, Mayr et al. explained that the features used to distinguish K. fordycei from K. biceae fall within the range of variation of a single species in modern penguins and the coeval extinct genus Muriwaimanu.

facts.statement: Kumimanu biceae is the type species of the genus Kumimanu.
facts.quote: type_species: Kumimanu biceae

facts.statement: The genus Kumimanu includes the species K. biceae and the proposed species K. fordycei.
facts.quote: subdivision: *K. biceae Mayr et al., 2017 K. fordycei Ksepka et al., 2023

facts.statement: Kumimanu is classified within the family Spheniscidae.
facts.quote: familia: Spheniscidae

facts.statement: Kumimanu is considered one of the largest known penguin species.
facts.quote: Kumimanu is one of the largest known penguins.

facts.statement: Kumimanu biceae is estimated to have reached a total length of 177 cm and weighed approximately 101 kg.
facts.quote: K. biceae is estimated to have reached 177 cm in total length from the tip of the beak to tail, and weighed around 101 kg.

facts.statement: The size of Kumimanu is surpassed only by the penguin genus Palaeeudyptes.
facts.quote: Its size is surpassed only by Palaeeudyptes, which reached a total length of up to 2 m and a body mass of 116 kg.

facts.statement: Kumimanu is older than any other previously discovered giant-sized penguin remains.
facts.quote: Kumimanu is older than all other previously found remains of penguins which reached 'giant' sizes

facts.statement: Kumimanu biceae measured approximately 1.60 to 1.77 meters in height and weighed over 91 kg, making it the second largest known penguin at the time of its description.
facts.quote: Mide aproximadamente cinco pies y tres a diez pulgadas (1,60 a 1,77 m) de altura y pesa más de doscientas libras (91 kg), siendo por lo tanto el segundo pingüino más grande conocido hasta ahora.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that K. biceae likely lived in a manner similar to modern penguins.
facts.quote: El K. biceae probablemente era similar a los pingüinos de hoy en día en la forma en que vivían.

facts.statement: Due to its large size, K. biceae likely consumed larger prey than modern penguins.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estas "Aves Monstruosas" probablemente pudieron consumir presas más grandes debido a su tamaño.

facts.statement: Kumimanu biceae lived in New Zealand, which was subtropical for much of the Paleocene.
facts.quote: El Kumimanu biceae vivió en Nueva Zelanda, que fue subtropical durante gran parte del Paleoceno.

facts.statement: The time range for Kumimanu is estimated from 59.24 to 56 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Thanetian to Thanetian (59.24 to 56 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The Kumimanu fossil is 55 million years old, living in the Paleocene, which is millions of years older than other previously found giant penguin remains.
rejected.quote: Este es un descubrimiento particularmente significativo porque el fósil tiene cincuenta y cinco millones de años, lo que significa que vivió en la era del Paleoceno, que es muchos millones de años más antiguo que todos los demás restos de pingüinos encontrados anteriormente que alcanzaron tamaños gigantes
